newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian markets take heart after Yeltsin surgery.
newsitem.headline: Russian markets take heart after Yeltsin surgery.

text.p: Short-term traders, betting on a full recovery by President Boris Yeltsin from heart surgery, pushed up prices in Russian markets and began a rally expected to last into next week, analysts said on Wednesday.

Some share prices were marked up a couple of percent before trade started as dealers reacted to further news of Yeltsin's health in anticipation of follow-through buying. But the market as a whole gained less than one percent over the day.
But markets, like Yeltsin, who met Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin during the day, are seen gathering energy quickly when they reopen on Sunday after a three-day holiday.
"In this country you have a coup one day, and three days later everybody says 'Great, we've survived'," said Flemings Moscow general manager Mark Jarvis.
Yeltsin had a successful quintuple bypass on Tuesday and resumed his full presidential authority on Wednesday, though doctors say the next week will be an important recovery period.

Russian MinFin bonds gained up to half a point on Tuesday's close and dealers said that a government call to clear up discrepancies in Russian law over $74 million in bonds frozen by police could lift the market further in later sessions.
"Prices have been rising the whole day just because Yeltsin feels all right and is likely to return to work quite soon," one MinFin dealer said.
The Treasury bill market looked ready to shave a percent or more from yields, especially on long paper, though computer problems delayed afternoon trade.
The yield on a new issue of six-month T-bills fell to 54.06 percent at auction on Wednesday from 58.46 a week ago.

Some dealers said shares could rise as much as five to 10 percent over the next week from Tuesday's prices, especially among second-tier and preferred stocks which have more room for growth and are gaining acceptance by foreign investors.

But many analysts said strength across markets over the next week would be based on short-term traders who expect to take profits soon, as demand from larger, longer-term investors increased, assuming Yeltsin staged a full recovery.

"There is an important period for speculation on all Russian markets. New real money will appear on the market only after the situation with Yeltsin is clear," said Alliance-Menatep chief debt trader Dmitry Falkovich.

New major investors, especially in fixed income, will watch for indications of economic health, such as the yield on Russia's forthcoming Eurobond and talks with an International Monetary Fund team coming to Moscow around November 14.
"The fundamentals this week are just as bad as two weeks ago," said a senior trader in Moscow who pointed to a lack of cash in the economy, strikes, and low tax collection.
But high expectations by some investors and caution among others are unlikely to lead to major corrections, analysts said.

Even if new investors hesitate, markets, led by volatile shares, have not inflated on expectations as they did in the run-up to Yeltsin's re-election in early July, which was followed by a market crash when long-term investors took profits from speculators.

Share prices are far below their high of July 4, when the RTS index reached 227.79. Wednesday's 184.35 was near the 185.00 level on September 4, just before Yeltsin announced he would have heart surgery, and investors are looking well ahead.
"The market is anticipating a positive resolution to these problems, maybe six to nine months down the road," the senior trader said.
